title: A 19-Year-Old Just Won the French Open—and Thanked Herself!
summary: Imagine you're 19 years old, standing on a huge clay court in Paris, and you just won one of the biggest tennis tournaments in the world. That's exactly what happened to Mirra Andreeva on Saturday! She beat Maja Chwalinska 6-3, 6-2 to win the French Open. Andreeva is from Russia, and she's the youngest player to win this title since Monica Seles did it way back in 1992. When Andreeva hit the winning shot, she threw her racket into the air and fell to her knees on the clay. During the trophy ceremony, she did something unusual: she thanked herself! She said, "I believed in myself and always gave 100 percent, even when it was tough." Her opponent, Chwalinska, joked that Andreeva's talent was "so annoying." Andreeva has been a star since she was 15. But lately, she's had to play without her country's flag because of the war with Ukraine. In the semifinals, a Ukrainian player refused to shake her hand. Still, Andreeva stayed focused and won. She even spoke a little French to the crowd, which made everyone cheer. The men's final is on Sunday, but for now, Andreeva is the queen of the clay.
why_it_matters: Mirra Andreeva shows that even young people can achieve big dreams by working hard and staying confident, just like when you prepare for a school competition or sport.
